Elena Mendez: Proposal: a lightweight per-token 'fidelity score' signal to guide aggressive 4-bit/FP8 sections inside a generation. Useful for long responses where early tokens are safe but later tokens risk hallucination.
Ravi Kapoor: Interesting. So we could switch precision mid-sequence? That complicates KV cache & kernel selection.
Sam O'Neil: Runtime implications: hot-swapping quant kernels mid-request requires saving/restoring per-layer scales. Might add 0.5-1ms/token overhead. Is that acceptable?
Tara Lin: For long generations (>256 tokens) that overhead amortizes. For short ones, we keep single-precision variant.
Elena Mendez: Score inputs: prefix SNR, token-level surprisal delta, attention mass spread, and task-specified flags (e.g., "code" vs "chit-chat").
Ravi Kapoor: Need a protocol: score_thresholds for switching to safer precision and hysteresis window to avoid flapping.
Sam O'Neil: Suggest hysteresis: require N consecutive tokens > threshold before switching, and cooldown of M tokens before allowing reverse.
infra-bot: Note: we must ensure memory layout compatibility between quant kernels; otherwise we'll need copy-on-write for KV storages.
Tara Lin: Also consider quant compaction: switching to low-bit requires different activation storage. Could do on-GPU in-place if we reserve max size upfront. Tradeoff: higher baseline memory.
Elena Mendez: Proposal for initial experiment: emulate mid-sequence switching in offline sampler (no kernel swaps) by stitching segments: run prefixed low-bit then suffix safer variant and compare to continuous fp32 baseline.
Ravi Kapoor: Good. If we see quality gains and acceptable perf, we can work on runtime support.
Sam O'Neil: Testing checklist:
- latency microbench for switching vs single-variant
- memory footprint with reserved max-buf approach
- correctness tests for KV continuity
- integration with batching logic (batches with mixed-switch points)
Tara Lin: Also add signal surface: `quant.fidelity_score`, `quant.switch_decision`, `quant.switch_reason`, `quant.switch_cooldown`.
Elena Mendez: Owners: offline stitcher + analysis - me. Runtime feasibility prototype - Sam. Kernel memory layout analysis - Ravi. Dashboards - Tara.
ops-bot: Available GPU slot: staging-cluster 04:00-08:00 UTC for 6h.
Elena Mendez: Timeline: offline stitch runs this week. If promising, runtime prototype next sprint.
Ravi Kapoor: Decision: run offline stitch experiment first. If delta metric < target threshold, stop. Otherwise invest in runtime.
Sam O'Neil: I'm adding unit tests that simulate KV continuity with simulated in-place compaction.
Tara Lin: I'll create a dashboard template and a Slack alert for sudden increase in switch rate (could indicate instability).
Elena Mendez: Thanks team, will post experiment artifacts when ready.
